taskVersion.name: ves-synthetic-a-item

parts.text:
Curve-type notation for vertical electrical sounding (VES): take the layer resistivities in depth order. For each group of three consecutive layers (layers 1-2-3, then 2-3-4, and so on), write one letter: A if r1 < r2 < r3; Q if r1 > r2 > r3; H if r1 > r2 < r3; K if r1 < r2 > r3. A curve with N layers gets N-2 letters, in depth order (for example, a 4-layer curve gets 2 letters, such as HA). If all the letters are the same, the curve may also be written as that single letter (AAA may be written A).

Station T-08, survey area T. Interpreted layer model:

Layer | Resistivity (ohm-m) | Thickness (m) | Depth to base (m)
----- | ------------------- | ------------- | -----------------
1 | 225.6 | 4.98 | 4.98
2 | 217.6 | 7.63 | 12.61
3 | 626.8 | 19.10 | 31.71
4 | 694.3 | 0.32 | 32.03
5 | 580.5 | - | -

What is the curve type of this station? Give a short answer, then end with one JSON line exactly like this:
{"curve_type": "<letters>"}

To determine the curve-type notation, we first identify the resistivity values for each layer:
$\rho_1 = 225.6$
$\rho_2 = 217.6$
$\rho_3 = 626.8$
$\rho_4 = 694.3$
$\rho_5 = 580.5$

With 5 layers, we need $N-2 = 3$ letters, corresponding to three consecutive groups of three layers:

1.  **Layers 1-2-3**: Comparing $\rho_1, \rho_2, \rho_3$
    $225.6 > 217.6 < 626.8$
    The pattern is (decrease, increase), which corresponds to **H**.

2.  **Layers 2-3-4**: Comparing $\rho_2, \rho_3, \rho_4$
    $217.6 < 626.8 < 694.3$
    The pattern is (increase, increase), which corresponds to **A**.

3.  **Layers 3-4-5**: Comparing $\rho_3, \rho_4, \rho_5$
    $626.8 < 694.3 > 580.5$
    The pattern is (increase, decrease), which corresponds to **K**.

Combining these, the curve type is HAK.

{"curve_type": "HAK"}
